instruction:
Work from a CalculiX cantilever template `/home/user/Desktop/beam_template.inp`. Use `/usr/bin/ccx` for the solve.

Build the stepped beam used in this series and run TWO load cases inside ONE job, then generate `/home/user/Desktop/solution.inp`:
- 11 nodes at `(10*(i-1), 0, 0)`, i = 1..11, and 10 B31 elements where element e joins nodes `e` and `e+1`
- Sections by region: elements 1-5 use a `10x10 mm` RECT section; elements 6-10 use a `6x6 mm` RECT section, assigned through element sets of your choice
- Material E=210000, nu=0.3; clamped boundary at node 1 (dofs 1-6)
- Step 1: apply FY=-100 N at node 11
- Step 2: apply FY=-200 N at node 11 (reset the loads with `*Cload, OP=NEW` so the second step carries only the new value)
- Request the nodal displacements in both steps (`*Node Print, NSET=...`, which needs an explicit node set)

Submit the single job with `ccx` and produce `/home/user/Desktop/solution.dat` containing results for both steps.

Write `/home/user/Desktop/summary.txt` as two comma-separated numbers: `uy_100, uy_200` — the vertical displacement of node 11 under the -100 N and the -200 N load cases.
